description: Apparently 'cultic objects' of a Roman date have been recovered from the building structure of St. Gabriel's chapel. It has been suggested as plausible that they derive from a private shrine from within a Roman townhouse. But it is uncertain if this should be the same location as Gabriel's chapel.
bibliography: Helm, R, and et al. Outside the Town: Roman Industry Burial and Religion at Augustine House Rhodaus Town Canterbury. Canterbury Archaeological Trust Occasional Paper 10. Canterbury Archaeological Trust, 2014.

Rady, J. “Excavations around St Gabriel’s Chapel, Canterbury Cathedral.” In Excavations in the Cathedral Precincts, 2 Linacre Garden, “Mesiter Omers” and St Gabriel’s Chapel. The Archaeology of Canterbury 4, 1990.
